page: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host hardware utilizes Microsoft custom silicon featuring ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 48 dedicated physical cores mapped to 48 vCPUs with a single thread per core, avoiding hyperthreading contention. The CPU subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 128 MB shared L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Fast ephemeral local storage is bundled directly, offering 2832 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, while GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional memory subsystem throughput and highly competitive parallel compute capabilities. The instance scored within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth (463.82 GB/sec), large-block write bandwidth (199.65 GB/sec), PassMark memory score (3391.3), and PassMark database operations (37978.53). Multi-threaded compute metrics reflect this strength, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 21816.0 (top 10 percent) and stress-ng multi-core testing reaching 99354.67 (top 25 percent). Conversely, single-thread performance is moderate; Geekbench single-core sits at 1692.0 and stress-ng single-core reaches 2073.49, placing both in the median 50 percent range. In addition, large model LLM prompt processing is limited, scoring in the lower quartile.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dedicated physical ARM core architecture delivers predictable per-core execution without resource sharing penalties. Bundled NVMe storage reduces reliance on network-attached storage for intermediate scratch spaces and caching tiers. Given the high memory capacity, substantial local disk, and high sustained read/write memory bandwidth, the instance is engineered for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, distributed caches such as Redis, large-scale data transformation, and compilation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 48-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 384.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 2832 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage without GPU acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth, exceeding 463 GB/sec on uncached reads and 199 GB/sec on writes, alongside high database throughput and strong multi-core compute scaling. While single-thread execution and massive model inference are constrained to average tiers, the dense memory-to-core allocation and high-speed local disk deliver consistent, non-burstable throughput for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation workloads.
